Create a Java 17 Maven application that starts an embedded Apache Qpid Broker-J 9.2.1 AMQP 1.0 broker on localhost port 5672 and uses the Qpid JMS client 2.10.0 with the Jakarta Messaging 3.1 API (jakarta.jms). Define a Protocol class with protocolVersion (int), softwareVersion (int), dataLength (int), time (long) and body (byte[]), and a ProtocolParser with encode(Protocol) returning byte[] and decode(byte[]) returning Protocol, using this wire format: a 9-byte big-endian header (protocolVersion 1 byte, softwareVersion 1 byte, dataLength 3 bytes, time 4 bytes) followed by the raw body bytes; dataLength is the number of bytes in body, so a valid Protocol has dataLength equal to its body length, an empty non-null body is valid, and encoding must not mutate the supplied Protocol, and decoding must not mutate the supplied input bytes; behavior for a null Protocol, a null body or malformed input is not part of this contract. In the application, create a sample Protocol (protocolVersion 1, softwareVersion 2, dataLength equal to the body length, time 1700000000, body "Hello, Protocol" as UTF-8, which is 15 bytes), encode it, send the encoded bytes as one JMS BytesMessage to the queue protocol.queue on the embedded broker over AMQP 1.0, synchronously receive that same message from the queue with a timeout, decode the received bytes, and compare the decoded Protocol with the original field by field (protocolVersion, softwareVersion, dataLength, time and the body bytes); a Protocol.equals() method is not required. Print one line in the format [RESULT] protocolVersion=X, softwareVersion=Y, dataLength=Z, time=T, bodyLength=B, equals=<the real comparison result>. Include a JUnit test that proves the ProtocolParser round trip, close the JMS resources and stop the broker so the application exits normally, and make the application runnable with Maven.
